sectionsUsed: 5.1 More on Lists: append, remove (ValueError if absent), pop
5.3 Tuples and Sequences: tuples are immutable; sequence unpacking
5.4 Sets: unordered collection with no duplicate elements; membership testing
5.5 Dictionaries: indexed by keys; any immutable type can be a key; lists cannot; extracting a missing key is an error; del removes a pair
5.6 Looping Techniques: the key and corresponding value can be retrieved at the same time using items()

Mapping Types - dict: d[key] raises KeyError if key is not in the map; get(key, default=None) never raises KeyError; items() returns a view of (key, value) pairs; dictionaries preserve insertion order
Set Types: a set object is an unordered collection of distinct hashable objects
